payload.rebuttal: argued: _drive adds a candidate's id to `passed_over` before it ever calls `on_passed_over`, and `passed_over` membership excludes that id from every later selection regardless of what the hook returns. The probe's lambda only removes the one id already excluded from a fresh copy of `follow_up_candidates`; its return value can never change which candidate `_drive` picks next, for any ordering of follow-ups, since the follow-up pass's own rescan hands back the same unfiltered list after the next real task anyway. I traced several orderings (over-budget first, last, two in a row) and every one lands on an identical outcome with or without the hook, and I ran the full suite (5029 tests) with the probe applied and nothing failed. The property the spec cares about, that a follow-up miss is not a layer miss, has no observable channel through run_stack_batch's return value because follow-up specs never carry depends_on, so no missed-layer recording could ever surface as a visible refusal downstream. The one hook that would matter, the real record_budget_miss built for the order's pass, does crash when wired to a follow-up (ValueError: list.remove(x): x not in list, since a follow-up candidate is never in remaining), and my existing test_a_follow_up_its_budget_cannot_cover_is_passed_over_and_the_next_one_runs test already catches that realistic mistake. The probe's lambda was built specifically to avoid touching missed or remaining, which is what makes it provably inert rather than a believable wrong implementation, and I see no way to kill it through run_stack_batch's public interface without adding introspection into its private closures.
